content:
The Wall Street Journal’s conservative editorial board has called for a Republican reckoning following what it described as the “crushing verdict” delivered by voters in the 2026 midterm elections.

In an editorial titled “The Trump Reckoning Arrives,” published in the early hours of Wednesday after Democrats were projected to regain control of both the House and Senate, the board argued that “this was more than a normal defeat.”

And it warned of lasting consequences for the GOP.

“The loss of Senate seats and governorships in states that had become GOP redoubts will have ramifications for years to come. So will the cascading losses down ballot in state legislatures,” it said.

President Donald Trump is “already blaming everyone else, but he is the main architect of this rout,” the board argued, adding that he was “directly responsible for at least three Senate defeats.”

The president’s “erratic and self-indulgent second-term governance alienated much of the coalition he assembled in 2024,” it continued, citing voter frustration and anger over the affordability crisis, persistent inflation and his war on Iran, themes the newspaper has taken Trump to task over on multiple occasions.

The sheer scale of the defeat calls “for soul-searching,” the board concluded, arguing that the GOP “needs a debate about what it stands for after Donald Trump.”
